chunk_map.heading: Pick one threat, record the decision (H1/lede)
Phase 1: Run the threat scan across your mapped surface
Read the threat list, expect more than you'll use
Phase 2: Pick the one threat worth hardening against
Push back on the incident story, land the mitigation
Phase 3: Write the decision as an ADR
Read the ADR, check the voice and the lens
Ask whether the ADR loads into future sessions
Save the map and the STRIDE walk before you clear

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a referent never named strands a reader mid-deck. Grepped body_numbered for pronouns/demonstratives across all 10 chunks. Chunk 1 line 22 'the access-surface map you built' -- session-artifact carve-out (student's own Ex1 output) AND arc-earned: earn-the-trust.md line 37 places 'Map the access surface' immediately before this file (line 39) in module include order. Chunk 1 line 20 'It runs in fresh context' resolves to 'the subagent' two words earlier, same sentence. Chunk 3 line 37 'you assess whether it fits' -- 'it' = the incident story, named in the same sentence's subject. Chunk 5 line 53 'its alternatives' -- 'its' = the ADR, named in the header at line 49 and the line's own opening clause. Chunk 6 lines 63-64 'The Decision section' / 'the Alternatives considered section' resolve against chunk 5's fenced prompt template (Context/Decision/Consequences/Alternatives considered), which precedes chunk 6 in reading order -- fences are exempt from being flagged but still count as prior context a reader saw. Chunk 7 lines 68-69 'the M3 worktree' / 'the fork prompt' / 'the side-quest' are this module's own opening exercise (Open the side quest, earn-the-trust.md line 33, precedes this file), and 'the fork prompt' is unpacked in the same sentence ('called the worktree "the side-quest"'). No never-named, vague-with-full-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent found.

Harm: locating another file by deck position breaks depending on where the reader's deck starts. Chunk 1 line 22 names the map by its own content ('the access-surface map you built'), no file-position pointer. Chunk 7 lines 68-69 name 'the fork prompt' and unpack its content in the same sentence rather than locating it by position ('Exercise 1 said...' does not appear anywhere in the current body -- the prior '(path is earlier in this scrollback)' locator lives only inside the exempt prompt fence at line 24/29 in the expanded view and points at the student's own terminal, not at another file). No sentence points at a prior file solely by position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a stranded callback sends the student hunting for a cut beat. Read earn-the-trust.md's live include list directly: line 33 'Open the side quest', line 37 'Map the access surface', line 39 this file, line 41 'Author your test-strategy skill'. This file's two implicit backward references -- 'the access-surface map you built' (chunks 1, 9) and 'the M3 worktree'/'the side-quest' (chunk 7) -- both resolve to beats confirmed present at that exact module position. The forward reference in the closer (line 89, 'The next exercise authors a test-strategy skill') checks out against line 41.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a guess/predict beat whose answer is narrated above it teaches nothing. The only ask-then-reveal shape in the file is chunk 8: the ask (line 74 + the fenced prompt at line 76) precedes the reveal (line 78, "Claude's answer: no...") in reading order, same chunk. No verbless-scene or terminal-pointing guess-cue found elsewhere -- this exercise has no live code-run demo beat at all (it is a discussion-and-draft exercise, not a run-and-observe one).

Harm: a slide with nothing standalone. Checked the thinnest chunks: chunk 2 (lines 29-30, 2 bullets) carries why the scan over-produces plus how to gauge scan depth; chunk 4 (lines 46-47, 2 bullets) carries the push-back rationale plus the land-the-mitigation instruction; chunk 6 (lines 63-64, 2 bullets) carries the voice-check plus the STRIDE-as-tool worked example. None is a bare wait-state fragment.

Harm: a header the body contradicts misleads a skimming reader. Checked all 9 '##' headers against their bodies, e.g. 'Check where the ADR landed' (line 66) -> body checks main-repo-vs-worktree path (lines 68-70); 'Ask whether the ADR loads into future sessions' (line 72) -> body asks then answers exactly that (74-79). Chunk 9's header ('Save the map and the STRIDE walk before you clear') covers lines 83-85 directly; the trailing 'What happened:'/'What this sets up:' widget lines are architecture-mandated closer chrome, not a second competing claim. No contradiction found.

Harm: cadence tics read as machine-authored on a slide. Ran `grep -noE 'Not [A-Za-z]+\. Not [A-Za-z]+\.'` against body_numbered -> zero hits ('One threat, not five' at line 36 is a single two-part contrast, not the banned triple). `grep -inE 'one of the (most|best)|most useful'` -> zero hits (no self-grading superlative). No anaphora/epistrophe triples anywhere in the file. No number+own-retraction (the four time budgets at lines 3, 17, 34, 51 are plain durations, no hedge). No abstraction-noun stacks (vocabulary stays concrete throughout: access surface, incident story, ADR, worktree, diff). No verb triplet with an empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: repo/authorial vocabulary a room can't parse. Ran `grep -noE '\b(compendium|firing|forcing function|beat|mood|Connections)\b'` against body_numbered (lines 1-90) -> zero hits (all such terms live only below the maintainer cut at line 91). 'Access surface'/'mapped surface' (line 7, chunk 1 header) is domain-standard security vocabulary (cf. attack surface) matching the rule's own carve-out for engineering-register terms, not authorial 'surface'-as-noun jargon. 'Main quest'/'side quest'/'worktree' are this module's own arc-earned teaching vocabulary (earned in this module's opener), not leaked internal dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: over-bolding trains readers to ignore bold as a signal. Ran `grep -noE '\*\*[^*]+\*\*'` against body_numbered -> 8 hits, all short (<=3 words) label chrome: chunk 0's **Time:**/**Window:**/**What you do:**/**What you build:**/**The point:**, chunk 9's **Worth keeping?**/**What happened:**/**What this sets up:**. The file's own 2026-07-09 emphasis-pass maintainer note (raw line 100) names this widget/label chrome as explicitly untouched per theory-plan.md's emphasis budget spec. No bolded whole-sentence narrative lead on any bullet across all 9 '##' chunks; no chunk exceeds the 1-narrative-bold budget.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: content invisible in the deck gets rules 1-9 applied to a slide that never renders. No phase-less bare-prose section exists in this file; the whole body sits under the single exercise wrapper. The rule-11/12/14 mechanical checks below ran directly against this file path via the shipped scripts and all returned per-file results, corroborating the deck recognizes it as a slide-bearing unit.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a declarative heading inside an exercise where none is earned muddies the imperative/phase-label mood exercises need. Checked all 9 '##' headings verbatim: 3 are 'Phase N: <label>' phase labels, 6 are imperative verb phrases ('Read the threat list...', 'Push back on the incident story...', 'Read the ADR, check the voice and the lens', 'Check where the ADR landed', 'Ask whether the ADR loads into future sessions', 'Save the map and the STRIDE walk before you clear'). None is a bare declarative claim; this exercise has no law/consolidation beat that would earn one. Consistent exercise mood throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a doctrine restatement / self-referential design note / aphorism kicker adds no move, object, tell, or priority the slide doesn't already hold. The diff since 9edae2ef already trimmed the closest near-miss (chunk 3's old middle sentence 'You are not inventing the worst case from scratch...' -- pure reassurance restating 'the agent proposes; you assess' -- is gone from the current body). Remaining candidate examined: chunk 2 line 29 'that rejection is the point, not a failure of the scan' echoes the lede's 'STRIDE's value is rejection, not enumeration' (line 11) but applies it at the exact moment the student feels the long list, adding a new instruction (don't mistake volume for shallowness) the lede doesn't carry -- kept, not redundant. No self-referential design commentary or aphorism-kicker instance found in the current body.
